title: Design a Todo List
summary: Design a per-user task manager: addTask creates a task with an increasing global id, description, due date and tags; getAllTasks and getTasksForTag return uncompleted tasks for that user ordered by due date; completeTask completes a task only for the user who owns it.
inputFormat: addTask takes user id, description, due date and tags; getAllTasks takes user id; getTasksForTag takes user id and tag; completeTask takes user id and task id.
outputFormat: addTask returns the task id; the list queries return task descriptions ordered by due date; completeTask return value not recorded.
tieRules: Tasks are ordered by due date; tie ordering is not recorded.
edgeRules: A different user cannot complete the task (draft).

examples.label: authored-reference
examples.input: addTask(1,'Finish report',5,['work']) -> 1; addTask(1,'Buy milk',2,['home']) -> 2; getAllTasks(1); completeTask(2,1); completeTask(1,1); getAllTasks(1)
examples.output: 1, 2, ['Buy milk','Finish report'], no effect, completed, ['Buy milk']
examples.note: Conditional on the return values of completeTask not being specified.

factsMissing: Tie ordering for equal due dates
Whether due dates are unique per user
questions: Can two tasks of the same user share a due date, and how are they ordered in the list results?
What does completeTask return, and does it return anything when the user is wrong?
